_README: TEMPLATE for the appsettings.Secrets.json that belongs to the test.gccwebapp.com SITE ONLY.
This is the sibling of appsettings.Secrets.template.json. That one is for gccwebapp.com, which
runs against the REAL production database. This one is for the second Plesk site, which runs
against the copy (gccwebap_test). Do not cross them.
WHY THIS FILE CARRIES THE CONNECTION STRING AND NOT JUST SECRETS
Both sites are deployed from the SAME zip, and that zip contains appsettings.Production.json
with the PRODUCTION connection string in it. Extracting the bundle into the test site's folder
therefore writes the production connection string into the test site, every single deploy.
appsettings.Secrets.json is the only config file that is NOT in the zip (Scripts/deploy.ps1
aborts if it reaches staging) and it is registered LAST (Program.cs:41), so it wins. Extracting
a zip adds and overwrites but never deletes, so this file survives every deploy untouched.
That makes it the correct - and only - durable place to point the test site at its own data.
THE FAILURE MODE THIS FILE PREVENTS, AND HOW IT LOOKS
If this file is missing, malformed, or the connection-string key is misspelled, the test site
silently falls back to appsettings.Production.json and starts reading and writing REAL CLIENT
RECORDS. Nothing errors. Every page loads. The data even looks right, because it is the real
data. This is the same silent-fallback shape as DEF-263 (empty SMTP creds -> MockEmailService).
VERIFY, DO NOT ASSUME. After every deploy and every app-pool recycle of the test site, read
the startup banner in logs\stdout:
Using SQL Server database provider
DB catalog : gccwebap_test        <-- MUST say gccwebap_test, never gccwebap_certificates
DB user    : <login>
If the catalog line says gccwebap_certificates, STOP. The test site is on production data.
HOW TO USE IT
1. Copy to appsettings.Secrets.json in the TEST SITE's folder, alongside GCCWebApp.dll.
Do NOT put this copy in the gccwebapp.com folder.
2. Fill in the real values and delete every _README / _comment key.
3. Recycle the test site's application pool.
4. Read the startup banner and confirm the catalog, per above.
Keep out of source control and out of deploy zips.
_comment_ConnectionStrings: Database=gccwebap_test is the whole point of this file. Everything else is optional.
If the existing GCC_adminxyz123 login was granted access to the copy, the ONLY difference
from the production string is the Database= value - copy the rest verbatim from
appsettings.Production.json. A dedicated login scoped to gccwebap_test is better practice:
it means a mistake in this file fails to CONNECT rather than succeeding against prod.
_comment_Jwt: GIVE THE TEST SITE ITS OWN SIGNING KEY. appsettings.Production.json ships one Jwt:Key to both
sites, so without this a token minted on the test site validates on gccwebapp.com and vice
versa - the two environments are not actually isolated at the token layer. Generate a fresh
64-byte base64 value; it does not need to be coordinated with anything.
_comment_DataProtection: Safe to set HERE and nowhere else. Changing ApplicationName on an EXISTING site makes every
outstanding auth cookie undecryptable and signs everyone out - which is why
appsettings.Production.json warns against touching it. The test site is brand new and has no
outstanding cookies, so naming it distinctly costs nothing and guarantees the two sites can
never share a key ring even if their folders are ever pointed at the same path.
_comment_TestEnvironmentGate: Optional. The gate is already Enabled=true in appsettings.Production.json, so the test site
inherits it and stays behind the password wall - which is what you want. Override the password
here only if you want the two sites to have different gate credentials.
_comment_SmtpSettings: admin@gccwebapp.com is the ONLY mailbox that exists on this mail server (verified by SMTP RCPT
probe 2026-08-19), so the test site logs in as the same mailbox and - via web.config /
appsettings.Production.json - sends From noreply@db.greencirclecertified.com, like the live
password-reset email sent from the test site is indistinguishable from one sent by
gccwebapp.com. Consider setting SmtpSettings:FromName to something like
'GCC Database - TEST' so a human can tell them apart in an inbox.
